title: CIF Ancient Systems Test Series (incorporating The Giza Transmission Hypothesis)
description: Sixteen disciplined, fully-cited case studies stress-testing the Coherent Inheritance Framework (CIF) against real archaeological and historical evidence. Series I (8 cases): the Giza pyramids, Aboriginal oral traditions, the Antikythera Mechanism, the Late Bronze Age Collapse, Japanese tsunami stones, Polynesian wayfinding, Gobekli Tepe, and undeciphered scripts. Series II (8 recovery cases, human-verified 2026-07-29): the Rosetta Stone, Linear B, Roman concrete, ancient music reconstruction, Wopanaak language reclamation, the Apollo F-1 engine, the BBC Domesday Project, and Greek Fire. Each study is falsifiable, separates established fact from inference and speculation, and ends with a shared verdict taxonomy and mandatory falsification check. Includes the framework document, methodology disclosure, cross-disciplinary grading review, and two syntheses. CIF is a candidate cross-domain framework (formerly Unified Inheritance Physics, UIP); it is offered as a structured vocabulary and set of design propositions, not as established physics.
notes: Version 2.2.0 adds Series II (recovery systems): 8 new case studies examining what can be recovered after a break, plus Series II synthesis and project-wide METHODOLOGY.md. Series II received a human-directed verification pass on 2026-07-29; corrections applied. Concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21618895 (always resolves to latest version). Most recent confirmed version before v2.2.0: v2.0.2 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21630213). Foundational Giza case study: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21618896.
